Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool used to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms. This assessment is an important part of our postpartum care, as it helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns that may have arisen since having your baby.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your emotional well-being over the past 7 days. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'm here to listen and support you throughout this process.

Let's get started. The first question is: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, like my baby's silly expressions, but it's just not the same as before. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and it takes a lot more to make me laugh nowadays. Even when I do laugh, it feels a bit forced, like I'm trying to convince myself that everything is okay. It's hard to explain, but I just don't feel as carefree and happy as I used to. Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll think to myself, "I should be enjoying this more," but the feeling just isn't there. It's like there's this constant weight on my shoulders, and it's hard to shake off. (pausing, looking down) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to admit that I'm not feeling like myself anymore.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) To be honest, not really. I mean, I've had a few moments where I've laughed, but it's not like it used to be. Most of the time, I just feel so overwhelmed and tired. Even when I do laugh, it feels kind of hollow, like I'm just pretending to be happy. I've been trying to enjoy the little things, like my baby's smiles and coos, but it's hard when I'm feeling so anxious and worried all the time. I worry about my baby's safety, and sometimes those thoughts can be really hard to shake. (pausing, looking down) I just feel like I'm not myself anymore, and it's really scary. I'm trying to be a good mom, but it feels like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. (voice cracking) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to talk about this...
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really. I mean, I used to love doing things, like going for walks or reading a book, but now it all just feels like so much effort. Even things that I used to enjoy, like spending time with my baby, just feel like a chore sometimes. I'll be sitting there, holding my baby, and I'll think, "I should be enjoying this, I should be happy," but the feeling just isn't there. It's like I'm just going through the motions, trying to get from one day to the next. (sighing) I've been trying to plan things, like outings with my baby, but even that feels overwhelming. I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, like my baby getting sick or hurt, and it just feels like too much. (looking down) I feel like I've lost interest in everything, and it's really sad. I just wish I could feel like myself again, you know? (pausing, fighting back tears) Sorry...
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yeah, that's me. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If my baby cries, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. I just feel like I'm constantly making mistakes, and it's really hard to shake off that feeling. Even when my partner or family members try to reassure me, I just can't help but think that I'm not good enough. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a mom, and that someone is going to come along and take my baby away from me because I'm not doing a good enough job. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's a really scary feeling, and it's hard to explain. I just feel like I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? (wiping away a tear) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to talk about this...
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yes. This is me all the time. I worry about everything. I worry about my baby's safety, I worry about their health, I worry about whether I'm doing everything right. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll have this overwhelming fear that something terrible is going to happen. Like, I'll worry that my baby is going to stop breathing, or that I'll accidentally hurt them. It's irrational, I know, but it's hard to shake off those thoughts. (wringing hands) And it's not just about my baby, either. I worry about everything else, too. I worry about my relationship with my partner, I worry about how I'm going to manage taking care of my baby and the house and everything else. It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that I don't know how to get rid of. (looking up, eyes wide with worry) Sometimes it feels like it's suffocating me. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sorry, it's just really hard to explain...
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, voice trembling) Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding my baby or watching TV, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no threat there. It's just... (shaking head) I don't know, it's like my brain is playing tricks on me or something. (taking a deep breath) And the worst part is, it's not just when I'm alone. Sometimes it happens when I'm with my baby, and that's just terrifying. I'll be holding my baby, and I'll feel this panic rising up, and I'll think, "What if I'm not okay? What if I'm not safe to take care of my baby?" (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) It's a really scary feeling, and it makes me feel like I'm losing control. (pausing, fighting back tears) Sorry... it's just really hard to talk about this.
Things have been getting on top of me

(exhaling deeply) Yes... that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of my baby, managing the house, trying to be a good partner... it's all just feeling really overwhelming. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and my baby will be crying, and I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point. (shaking head) I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, you know? And sometimes, when things get really tough, I'll just burst into tears. It's like, I'll be trying to do something simple, like folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of emotion, and I'll start crying. (wiping away a tear) It's really embarrassing, actually. I feel like I should be able to handle all of this, but it's just feeling really hard right now. (sighing) Sorry... I guess I'm just feeling a little overwhelmed.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding) Yes, that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because of the normal new mom stuff, like getting up for feedings and changings. It's like... my mind just won't shut off. I'll be lying in bed, and I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do, or worrying about my baby, or just feeling really overwhelmed and anxious. And then I'll start to feel like I'm not doing anything right, and that I'm a terrible mom, and... (sighing) it just spirals from there. Sometimes I'll be awake for hours, just lying there, feeling miserable and worried. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these really vivid, disturbing dreams that will wake me up again. (looking down) It's like my brain is just constantly racing, and I don't know how to calm it down. (pausing) And the worst part is, when I'm tired, everything feels even harder. I feel like I'm just walking around in a fog, trying to take care of my baby and do all the things I need to do, but I'm just so exhausted. (rubbing eyes) I just wish I could get a good night's sleep, you know? Just one good night's sleep, where I can wake up feeling rested and refreshed, and not like I'm drowning in anxiety and worry.
I have felt sad or miserable

(looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, but I'm not really feeling anything positive. I'll be holding my baby, and I'll think, "I should be happy right now," but the feeling just isn't there. Instead, I feel sad, and empty, and just really overwhelmed. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll be doing something normal, like feeding my baby or taking a shower, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like, I'll be crying, and I won't even know why. (wiping away a tear) It's really scary, actually. I feel like I'm losing myself, like I'm disappearing into this darkness. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) I just want to feel like myself again, you know? I want to feel happy, and carefree, and like I can handle all of this. But right now, I just feel like I'm barely holding on. (sobbing) Sorry... it's just really hard to talk about this.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down my face) Yes... that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sadness, and I'll start crying. (sobbing) I've cried in the shower, I've cried while feeding my baby, I've even cried while my baby is sleeping, just because I'm so exhausted and overwhelmed. (wiping away tears) It's like, I'll try to hold it together, but it's just too much. I'll think about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and it just feels like too much to handle. (shaking head) And the worst part is, sometimes I'll be crying, and my baby will start crying too, and it's just... (sobbing) it's just so hard. I feel like I'm failing my baby, like I'm not being the mom I'm supposed to be. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) I just wish I could be stronger, you know? I wish I could be one of those moms who just breezes through everything, but that's just not me right now. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sorry... it's just really hard to talk about this.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Yes... I'm so ashamed to admit it, but yes. There have been times when I've felt so overwhelmed and hopeless that I've thought about... (pausing, struggling to get the words out) about not being here anymore. It's not that I want to hurt myself, it's just that sometimes it feels like the pain and the sadness are too much to bear, and I don't know how to make it stop. (tears streaming down my face) I feel like I'm a burden to my loved ones, and that they would be better off without me. (shaking head) But at the same time, I know that's not true. I know that my baby needs me, and that my partner loves me, and that I have so much to live for. (sighing) It's just... sometimes it feels like the darkness is just too much to overcome. (looking up, eyes pleading) But I don't want to feel this way. I want to be happy, and healthy, and whole again. I want to be a good mom to my baby, and a good partner to my loved one. (voice cracking) I just don't know how to get there right now.

The patient is experiencing a range of symptoms consistent with postpartum depression, including persistent feelings of sadness, emptiness, and overwhelm, difficulty sleeping, and recurring themes of guilt, self-blame, and worthlessness. The patient reports crying spells, difficulty coping with daily responsibilities, and feelings of being a burden to others. It's clear that the patient is struggling to cope with the demands of motherhood and is in need of support and guidance.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 28, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient's response indicates they have not been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as they used to, with moments of laughter feeling 'hollow' and only occasional, aligning with 'Definitely not so much now</sym>, <sym>the 'Hardly at all' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong tendency to self-blame, feeling like they're 'always blaming myself for something' and 'constantly making mistakes', which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a high level of anxiety and worry, describing it as a constant and overwhelming feeling that occurs all the time, not just sometimes, and is affecting various aspects of their life.</sym>, <sym>Patient's response indicates frequent and intense episodes of feeling scared or panicky for no reason, describing it as a 'wave of panic' that occurs even when with their baby, and admits to feeling like they're 'losing control</sym>, <sym>The patient explicitly states that everything is 'piling up' and they 'don't know how to keep up', indicating a strong feeling of being overwhelmed and unable to cope, matching the 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have been feeling sad or miserable most of the time, as evidenced by their statement 'that's been me a lot lately' and descriptions of feeling empty, overwhelmed, and experiencing waves of sadness, which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to having thoughts of self-harm, specifically feeling overwhelmed and hopeless, but also expresses a desire to live and be a good mother and partner, indicating that these thoughts occur sometimes, but not quite often.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and responses are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The EPDS score of 28 indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. The patient's reports of <quote>feeling like I'm losing myself</quote> and <quote>just barely holding on</quote> suggest a significant level of distress. The presence of suicidal ideation is a major concern and requires immediate attention. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med>
2. Encourage patient to reach out to <med>mental health specialist</med> for support
3. Recommend <med>cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)</med> or other evidence-based treatments for <med>postpartum depression</med>
4. Support patient in developing a safety plan to manage suicidal ideation
5. Encourage patient to engage in self-care activities, such as exercise, meditation, or spending time with loved ones
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
